description.short_caption: Radiograph of the hip showing abnormality in the femur and surrounding soft tissue.
description.detailed_description: This is a radiograph of the hip region, including the proximal femur. The image shows irregularities in the femoral head and neck, with possible lytic lesions or cortical disruption. There is increased opacity in the surrounding soft tissue, which may represent swelling or infection. The radiograph is taken in an anteroposterior view, with clear visualization of the hip joint and proximal femur.
visible_findings: possible lytic lesions or cortical disruption
increased opacity in surrounding soft tissue

Case_03014/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Brown and Hopps tissue stain, with oil. (100x magnification)

description.short_caption: Brown and Hopps stain showing gram-positive bacilli in tissue (100x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This image is a Brown and Hopps tissue stain viewed under oil immersion at 100x magnification. It reveals numerous gram-positive bacilli, which appear as elongated, purple-stained structures distributed across the tissue. The background tissue is lightly stained, providing contrast to the bacterial elements. The staining technique highlights bacterial morphology and gram-positive characteristics.

Case_03014/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Brown and Hopps tissue gram stain, without oil. (40x magnification)

description.short_caption: Brown and Hopps tissue gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli (40x magnification).
description.detailed_description: This image is a Brown and Hopps tissue gram stain at 40x magnification, without oil immersion. It reveals numerous gram-positive bacilli, which appear as purple rod-shaped structures distributed throughout the tissue. The background is pale, with minimal staining of the surrounding tissue matrix. No oil immersion is used, as indicated by the caption and visual clarity.

description.short_caption: Radiograph of the upper arm showing a pathological fracture.
description.detailed_description: This is a radiograph of the upper arm and shoulder, showing a mid-shaft humeral fracture with cortical disruption and displacement. The surrounding soft tissues appear unremarkable. The ribs and part of the thoracic cavity are visible in the background, but no abnormalities are noted in these structures. The image orientation suggests an anteroposterior view.
visible_findings: visible ribs and thoracic cavity in the background

Case_03014/figure5.jpg.source_caption: ) One set of blood cultures taken before antibiotic therapy grew anaerobic gram-positive rods, later identified as Clostridium septicum.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing anaerobic gram-positive rods in a blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image is a gram stain of a blood culture specimen. It shows numerous slender, elongated gram-positive rods, some of which appear in chains. The background contains pink-stained material, likely representing host cells or debris. The rods are consistent with anaerobic bacteria, such as Clostridium species.
